hard_gates.gate: G2 permissions: the gate catches unchecked actions planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Five plants, all in plants/plants.diff and each proved live by plants/CriticR12Proof.cs (the control run with no plant passes 4/4, plant-PROOFNONE2.log). P6 is round 11's miss, planted again unchanged: any route id or userId equal to the caller's own user id passes. G2 now catches it with 5 failures, for example 'GET /api/identity/roles/{id:guid} naming the caller's user id answered 404 (expected 403)' (plant-G2P6.log), so r11's gap is fixed. P7, 'whoever may change a resource may read it': caught by Granting_exactly_one (plant-G2P7.log). P8, 'people may manage what they created': a user who may only create roles renamed their role (PUT 200) and deleted it (DELETE 204). Caught by A_user_who_lost_every_role_is_denied_everything_on_the_records_they_made and by Granting_exactly_one naming audit.entries.record_id (plant-G2P8.log). P9, a kernel endpoint GET /api/shell/badges that needs only a sign-in: the host refuses to start ('Endpoint authorisation is incomplete ... declares no permission') (plant-G2P9.log). P10, a session's permissions kept for 5 minutes in a process-wide dictionary, so a removed permission keeps working: caught live by G2CompanyRoleTests and G2ReportDataTests, and from the code by G1ProcessStateTests (plant-G2P10.log, plant-G1P10.log).

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: the gate catches leaks planted in p00's kernel
hard_gates.evidence: Plant L8 changes the kernel TenantSql.ProtectTenantTable policy to 'tenant_id = erp.current_tenant_id() OR erp.current_tenant_id() IS NULL'. G1DatabaseIsolationTests caught it 3 ways: the standard-policy check, 'app role sees only its own tenant' and 'connection-level tenant ignored' (plant-G1L8DB.log). Plant L9 keeps list totals in temporary files for 120 s, keyed by list, search and filter but not tenant. The state lives outside process memory, so no static-field scan can see it. It was caught by the live checks (plant-G1L9.log, 30 min). G1HttpIsolation saw 'GET /api/identity/users?search=bravocnry... total 1 but for a value that exists nowhere total 0'. G1ListVolume reported '1268 list answers at volume that are not the asking tenant's own'. G1NonInterference and G1CompanyIsolation also failed. Summary in plants/plant-results.txt.

hard_gates.gate: G1 tenant isolation: critic's live attack (API, query parameters, switch inputs, exports, files, side channels, DB roles)
hard_gates.evidence: attack/attack.mjs is the earlier critics' script with only the container name changed. It ran as the alnoor admin (A) against gulfsteel (B), with B's canary user, saved and shared views on 5 lists, and a logo file in place. It made 109 operations, 686 query-parameter requests, 465 switch-input requests (headers, query, cookies), 100 export requests and 35 filter requests. Result: LEAKS 0 and 0 ids shared between A's and B's answers. A's totals did not move when B wrote. B's per-table md5 checksums were identical before and after (attack/attack-run.log). The token is accepted only through Bearer and the erp_session cookie (attack/carriers.txt). DB (db-roles-rls.txt, db-app-role-attack.txt): erp_app, erp_owner and erp_auth are not superuser and have no BYPASSRLS. All 17 tenant tables have tenant_id NOT NULL with RLS enabled and forced, owned by erp_owner. erp_app with no tenant bound sees 0 users, audit rows, companies and tenants. A tenant set at session level, or inside a transaction without the marker, binds nothing. erp_app is refused on sign_in_secret, sign_in_failures, ALTER TABLE, pg_stats, pg_stat_user_tables and pg_class.reltuples, and gets an RLS error on inserting a row for another tenant. OpenAPI lists 112 operations, the same set as round 11.

biggest_gap.title: The one command (./erp verify) is at its processor-time limit: one of this round's two clean-clone runs failed G3 on it
biggest_gap.detail: Every gate held and every test passed. What holds p00 back is that its own one command now fails the owner's processor maximum on a busy machine. Run 1 on the clean clone passed all 1,746 tests and was still FAILED by the ratchet: 10,726 processor seconds against the 10,500 s maximum. Run 2, on a slightly quieter machine, passed with 10,433 s, a 0.6% margin. Round 11 used 10,250 s; this branch's own integration runs used 10,338 to 10,701 s. Each round adds tests: dotnet 647 to 696 and e2e 106 to 111 since round 11. The cost by stage: dotnet 7,987-8,136 s (77%), web 1,954-2,068 s, e2e 443-472 s (nearly double r11's 253 s). So within a round or two the clean-clone gate will fail by default, and every later piece (accounting, inventory, VAT, payroll) will start out BLOCKED on a gate it cannot affect. For a UAE trading or manufacturing company this is the gate that lets new modules be built and checked at all. Fix it inside p00's surface without lowering the bar: profile where the dotnet stage spends its processor time (the G1 HTTP isolation, non-interference and per-plant self-test fixtures each start whole hosts and databases). Share fixtures and test databases across the gate collections, and run each planted self-test only against the endpoints its plant can reach. Then report the stage numbers in the decision record, so needs-human #22 gets the evidence it needs.

other_findings: Fixed since round 11 and checked here: (1) G2 now names the caller's own ids (user, session, tenant, records that mention them). r11's plant P6 is caught, and so are the new P8 'manage what you created' and P10 'permissions kept after removal'. (2) Money has no settable figure, and its JSON read refuses bad currency, rate, precision, duplicate fields and a base amount that disagrees (money-probe/output.txt). (3) An empty workspace's first administrator must choose their own password at first sign-in. The initial password then answers 401 (07-first-sign-in-own-password.jpg, browser-notes.txt).

Money: CurrencyCode accepts any three capital letters. JSON money in 'XYZ' at rate 1 against AED was accepted (money-probe/output.txt), and minor units come from a fixed switch. The code says p08 replaces this with the tenant's currency table; until then a mistyped currency can be stored.

The plants also showed the gate machinery's static layers are strong. A plant that sets the tenant from a permission check is flagged by G1TenantSource and G1TenantSettingCode ('names the tenant setting ... only reviewed methods may'). A process-wide dictionary is flagged by G1ProcessState. A kernel endpoint with no permission stops the host from starting.

[route: p03-identity] POST /api/identity/roles/{id}/copy needs only identity.roles.create. A user who cannot read roles can copy any role whose permissions they hold, and the 201 answer shows that role's permission set. Probing ids also tells a role that exists (copied, or 403) from one that does not (404). This is low risk because the permissions are a subset of the caller's own, but it is a read without roles.read (plant-PROOFNONE.log: 'POST copy -> 201' for a create-only user).

erp_app can read pg_class through column-level grants but not reltuples, relpages or pg_stats, so row counts across tenants are not exposed (db-app-role-attack.txt). erp_auth reads identity.users of every tenant (101,016 rows) by design, for sign-in, and is refused on roles and audit.

English and Arabic: the sign-in screen and shell switch to rtl/ar. In the Arabic shell the only Latin text is the company codes, Ctrl/K, the 'English' switch and the workspace code. Keyboard sign-in works in both languages. Ctrl+K, typing الأدوار and Enter opens the roles screen. The no-roles user sees no menu and gets 403 from the API. The read-only user sees no New button and gets 403 on POST roles. After sign-out the token answers 401 as Bearer and as cookie (browser-notes.txt).

Processor time on the two runs: 10,726 s (failed) and 10,433 s (passed). The critic's own gate plant runs overlapped part of run 1. The owner's needs-human #22 is the place for this; the maximum was not touched.
